condition: recurrent dark red gross hematuria with small blood clots on 3 voiding episodes over 2 weeks in a 64-year-old former dye factory worker
level_rationale: Passing dark red urine containing small blood clots on 3 occasions over 2 weeks in a 64-year-old man with occupational dye-factory exposure is visible gross hematuria with high urothelial malignancy risk requiring urology specialist cystoscopy and CT urography, whereas having medium-yellow first morning urine once yesterday morning reflects ordinary physiologic overnight urine concentration requiring no medical care.

Observation involves his urine when voiding
Has passed dark red urine with small blood clots 3 times over 2 weeks

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain low-literacy older male lexical register swap (-reg, Wiktionary) + uncontracted beet-color causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact urine appearance de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive-wording reference facts (64-year-old man who worked in a dye factory, voiding observation, and 3 episodes over 2 weeks of dark red urine with small blood clots) with zero contractions, zero stated negatives ('painless' omitted), and an exact 16-vs-16 word span swap. Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 on voiding to medium-yellow first morning urine once yesterday morning shifts care cleanly from urology specialist cystoscopy (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
